newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: China's CNPC to win stake in Kazakh oil firm.
newsitem.headline: China's CNPC to win stake in Kazakh oil firm.

text.p: A spokesman for Kazakhstan's State Privatisation Committee said on Tuesday that the Chinese National Petroleum Company (CNPC) was set to win a 60 percent stake in the Aktyubinskmunaigas oil enterprise.

"We are 90 percent sure that a contract will be signed with the Chinese tomorrow (Wednesday)," Merkhat Nigmatullin, spokesman for the committee, told reporters. The committee has said the enterprise sits on about 483 million tonnes of oil.

U.S. oil majors Texaco and Amoco Corp, along with Russian company Yuzhny Most, competed against CNPC in the tender. The committee said earlier that Exxon Corp of the United States had dropped out of the competition.

Aktyubinsk, located in the west of the former Soviet republic, is one of Kazakhstan's richest in terms of oil reserves. Official figures put its current annual production of crude oil at about 2.6 million tonnes (52,000 barrels per day).
Last month, Indonesia's Central Asia Petroleum paid the Kazakh government a $248 million bonus for a 60 percent stake in major oil producer Mangistaumunaigas and promised to invest over $4 billion.

The government has said it aims to finish a fast-track privatisation of the country's potentially rich but troubled oil industry by next month, against opposition from the enterprises' Soviet era managers.
